# Rules

Every rule that governs this repo, with its one home and what actually
checks it. `enforcement` is honest: **`prose` means nothing checks it** —
`gate` names the check that will.

## Rules

| Rule | Home | Scope | Principle | Enforcement | Gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Admission gate | CLAUDE.md#gate-run-first | repo | Every session and every commit records admission through the one gate script; a missing tool is restored, never worked around. | hook | — |
| Drift markers | https://github.com/popemkt/kb/blob/v0.3.0/AGENTS.md#drift-markers-and-gaps | repo | A deferred clean shape carries a GAP marker at the deferral site and a matching gap node naming expected, current, impact and closes. An unlabelled workaround is drift. | hook | — |
| Abstraction before addition (Rule 1) | https://github.com/popemkt/kb/blob/v0.3.0/AGENTS.md#rule-1--abstraction-before-addition | repo | Every change lands in the shape it would have had if the requirement had always existed; when the model does not fit, the model gets fixed, not special-cased. | prose | — |
| Canonical statements | https://github.com/popemkt/kb/blob/v0.3.0/AGENTS.md#canonical-statements | repo | Every rule, principle and decision has exactly one home; other files link to it and never restate it. Restatement is drift. | prose | — |
| Module boundaries | CLAUDE.md#module-boundaries | repo | A stack owns its slice end to end and decides package membership; an executor installs whatever lands in its channel and never decides per package. | prose | A flake check that no executor in modules/ names a package, only the channel it reads |
| One contract, every implementation | https://github.com/popemkt/kb/blob/v0.3.0/AGENTS.md#one-contract-every-implementation | repo | A behaviour one implementation of a port guarantees is a guarantee of the port: stated once in the spec and proved by one contract suite that runs over every implementation. | prose | A harness check that every port with more than one implementation has a contract suite run over its whole registry. Not built yet, because half the ports are not discoverable: the store and tail ports are nominal (class … implements), but the scene handle, the graph renderers and the design systems are object-literal registries, so a check over implements clauses alone would read as covering the rule while missing them. The first step is one registry form every port declares. Found while looking: storeContract and logContract run over JsonlStore and SqliteStore (and their tails), but not over the UI's BrowserStore or tx-log's MemoryTxTail. |

## Gaps

### GAP: agent-prompt review rules are not ported to this repo

- **expected** — The dotfiles skills and agent directory has a stated review checklist for every prompt or skill change, with the mechanical half actually checked.
- **current** — Nothing reviews agent prompts here. The reference repo's PROMPT_REVIEW_RULES.md (R1-R20) was measured as directly portable and deliberately left out of this wave.
- **impact** — Prompt and skill files accrete unreviewed; the load-bearing rules (do not compensate in prose for missing implementation; push determinism into code) are exactly the ones an agent breaks silently.
- **closes** — Decide the home for the checklist in this repo, port R1-R20, and wire the mechanical subset the way the reference repo does before adding more skills.
- **node** — `01M1M08W6Z70XV3KCQB5CWH3ZR`

### GAP: an imported Claude Code session is a new bb thread seeded with its transcript, not the session itself

- **expected** — bb adopts an existing Claude Code session as a thread: it resumes the provider session natively (same session id, full context, prompt cache), records thread/identity only after that resume succeeds, and binds the thread to the session's cwd on its machine.
- **current** — assets/bb-plugins/session-import spawns a fresh claude-code thread and hands it a cleaned, budgeted transcript (agent-only text plus the full transcript as a local file). bb 0.46.1 has no create-thread providerThreadId and no timeline append, so a plugin cannot adopt the session.
- **impact** — The new thread starts from a summary: older turns beyond the budget, tool outputs and images reach the agent only through the transcript file, the prompt cache starts cold, and the original session and the bb thread diverge from the first new message.
- **closes** — get-bb/bb#3260 (adopt an external Claude Code session) ships; session-import then calls it and keeps the transcript seed only as the fallback for providers or machines that cannot resume.
- **node** — `01M5YQ7EX8GTERS32BT5G9H7Q7`

### GAP: bb plugin settings cannot inherit a value or describe it live

- **expected** — A plugin setting can be left unset (inherit) from bb's UI, a boolean can be tri-state, and a description can show the effective value ("currently: wobbly, from ZZZ") next to the setting.
- **current** — bb 0.46.1 settings descriptors are static (registered once in server.ts); a stored value always shadows the default and the UI cannot unset it; a boolean is a two-state switch. bb-lively models From preset as an explicit select option (the default), turns its switches into From preset/On/Off selects, and shows effective values in its own Preset settings section.
- **impact** — Effect switches are dropdowns instead of switches; a stored boolean from before presets falls back to From preset (bb coerces a type mismatch to the default); effective values live in a section below the settings, not beside each one.
- **closes** — bb adds an inherit/unset state or dynamic descriptions to plugin settings; then bb-lively's adapter/settings.ts goes back to switches and per-setting descriptions.
- **node** — `01M5RXXJV7Q5EWQF8EVK8VFX85`

- **closes** — install on a bb host, walk the README's after-upgrade checklist (a thread, a menu, a dialog, a toast, Settings switches), read Selector health, try both themes in light and dark, then set this gap's status to done

### GAP: bb's idle gate cannot see past a daemon cut off from the server

- **expected** — app-bb-daemon's idle-gated restart happens once its threads finish, even while the daemon cannot reach the server
- **current** — The idleCheck asks the server (bb thread list). A daemon the server cannot see (the daemon down, or the server down for long) leaves its threads active in the server's database, so the check never passes. A protocol mismatch no longer causes this: both units run one pinned bb-app copy (app-npm-pin). The waiter gives up after 24 h and a timer retries hourly; restart-app --status, which rebuild prints, lists the pending restart
- **impact** — The daemon's restart waits until someone runs sudo systemctl restart app-bb-daemon
- **closes** — An idle check that also asks the daemon itself (its local API on 127.0.0.1:38887) or treats a disconnected daemon as idle; or an upstream bb way to list a daemon's running work
- **node** — `01M5P0D3VP9RXH16D7VJV282BT`

### GAP: bb's SDK cannot keep a thread panel tab mounted, so the kb plugin hoists its frames into an app overlay

- **expected** — A threadPanelAction can ask bb to keep its tab mounted (hidden, not unmounted) across thread switches and while inactive, or bb offers a window-level panel host, so a plugin's iframe survives without positioning tricks.
- **current** — @get-bb/plugin-sdk 0.6.49 (bundled-types/bb-plugin-sdk-app.d.ts): PluginThreadPanelActionRegistration is { id, title, icon?, component, layout?, run? } and PluginThreadPanelProps is { threadId, params }, with no keep-mounted option; experimental_appOverlay is the one slot mounted once per window. bb-app 0.47.0 (app/dist/assets): ThreadSecondaryPanel-*.js renders only the active tab (renderContent of the active one), and usePanelTerminals-*.js keys a plugin tab's mount by thread/<threadId>/<tab id>, so a thread switch destroys the tab. The kb plugin keeps one frame per recently shown thread (three) in an experimental_appOverlay (assets/bb-plugins/kb/frames.tsx), positioned fixed over the tab's placeholder by one shared animation-frame loop and clipped to the placeholder's clipping ancestors; hidden frames are visibility:hidden and inert, and only shown frames are reported as their thread's tab.
- **impact** — Depends on an experimental slot; a frame follows its place one animation frame late during panel resizes and moves; its z-index (35) is read from bb's bundled classes and must be checked again when bb changes its stacking; a fourth thread evicts the least recently shown kb tab.
- **closes** — bb ships a keep-mounted option for threadPanelAction (or a stable per-window panel host); then KbPanel renders its frame directly again and frames.tsx goes.
- **node** — `01M5QN6PKBQ5YE4FNB1PYPXR92`

### GAP: package executors share no contract check

- **expected** — Every executor-installed channel in modules/options/channels.nix names the executor view that installs it, and one flake check proves, per host, that each channel's members reach that view. A new executor joins the check by registering its view.
- **current** — Homebrew, npm, Bun and agent-plugins each read their channel their own way. The resolved views are ad hoc (homebrew.* for Homebrew, my.resolvedNpmGlobals and my.resolvedBunGlobals for npm and Bun, none for the Claude and Codex plugin channels), and only the drift audit, at runtime, compares them with the machine.
- **impact** — An executor that drops or filters channel members still evaluates and builds; the loss shows only as drift on a live machine after rebuild.
- **closes** — Replace the ad hoc resolved* options with one registry the executors fill per channel (npm-global.nix is part of this; it had uncommitted user edits when this was filed), then add an executor-contract flake check over channels.nix and point the drift audit at the same registry.
- **rule** — One contract, every implementation
- **node** — `01M3E9V4VV52HJPW181Y74AR0J`

- **node** — `01M5QJFW217ZNBXHEX74VG7VYP`

### GAP: the npm executor special-cases @openai/codex and aborts activation on a failed install

- **expected** — installNpmGlobals treats every member of my.pkgs.npmGlobals alike and warns and continues when an install fails, like installBunGlobals and agent-plugins.
- **current** — Its loop carries an elif for @openai/codex that runs npm rebuild when the codex bin link is missing, and a failing npm install -g aborts the rest of Home Manager activation.
- **impact** — The executor decides per-package behaviour, which Module Boundaries reserves for stacks, and one unreachable npm package blocks every later activation step.
- **closes** — Generalise the relink to any declared package whose bin links are missing (or move it to the owning stack), and add || warn to the install. The marker could not be placed: npm-global.nix had uncommitted user edits.
- **rule** — Module boundaries
- **node** — `01M3E9V5JS5VS5ZRT14510BN4D`

### GAP: The repo's Claude Code marketplace and agent skill links point into the person's checkout

- **expected** — What an agent loads from this repo is the revision applied, as bb plugins are since they install from the Nix store (modules/common/home-manager/bb-plugins/); in-place reading is an explicit opt-in for development.
- **current** — modules/stacks/ai-agents/claude-mods.nix declares the marketplace dotfiles=~/.dotfiles/assets/plugins, which Claude Code reads in place, and scripts/sync-agent-plugins.sh symlinks assets/plugins/*/skills into ~/.agents, ~/.claude, ~/.codex and ~/.cursor at the checkout. Chosen so an edit reaches a session with /reload-plugins and no reinstall. Darwin hosts only today.
- **impact** — Agents run whatever the checkout holds (a feature branch, uncommitted edits, a stale tree), not the applied revision; on a host several people apply from it would repeat the bb-lively downgrade of 2026-10-26.
- **closes** — Marketplace and skill links point at a store copy of assets/plugins (or a writable copy keyed by its hash, as bb plugins do), with a documented in-place mode for trying edits, like bb-plugins-sync --path.
- **node** — `01M5W9JKV26YK4R234A0F60X21`

### GAP: the stop indicator cannot tell a stop by the person from a stop by another agent

- **expected** — The why-this-thread-stopped badge says 'stopped by you' or 'stopped by another agent' (naming the agent's thread)
- **current** — bb 0.46.1 records a manual stop as system/thread/interrupted {reason: manual-stop} with no actor (start-server.js:18051-18054, events table :38133-38150), and POST /threads/:id/stop ignores the caller (:188417-188425), so the badge says 'you or an agent (bb does not record which)'
- **impact** — The owner cannot see at a glance whether a thread was stopped by hand or by an orchestrating agent
- **closes** — bb recording the stop's initiator (person, or the calling thread) on system/thread/interrupted or the stop route, then actorOf in assets/bb-plugins/restart-resume/core/stops.ts reading it
- **node** — `01M5P8BKXY41S86WZ468GS0109`

### GAP: the two pin tools use different could-not-run exit codes and no shared test holds them to one contract

- **expected** — github-sources and uv-sources implement one stated contract for check (0 current, 10 newer upstream, one code for could not resolve) and update, stated once, with a shared offline test that runs both against stubbed resolvers.
- **current** — uv-sources exits 1 when it cannot resolve, where github-sources exits 20; both use 0 for current and 10 for newer upstream releases. Only github-sources has an offline test (github-sources-check). The drift audit consumes both through report_pin_check, which treats any other code as skipped.
- **impact** — A caller that tells unresolvable apart from broken (as github-sources callers can with 20) gets a different answer from uv-sources, and nothing notices when the two diverge further.
- **closes** — State the pin-tool contract once in docs/github-release-packages.md, move uv-sources to exit 20 for could not resolve, and add a uv-sources case to a shared stubbed check next to github-sources-check. Coordinate with the owner of scripts/github-sources.
- **rule** — One contract, every implementation
- **node** — `01M3E9VSQZTDHRV4C9YRWD1QV1`

### GAP: three hand-copied uv tool installers, each reading a failed uv tool list as not installed

- **expected** — One uv tool installer (a shared helper each owning module calls with its spec, extras and extra freshness checks) that captures uv tool list, checks its exit status, and warns and continues on failure, as AGENTS.md Writing an executor requires.
- **current** — semantica.nix, cognee/server.nix and cognee/client.nix each repeat the same toolchain exports and uv tool install --force block, and each probes with uv tool list | grep -q, so a crashed uv reads as not installed and forces a reinstall. The copies already drifted once: the cognee checks matched hand-typed versions until 3d9e0bd0.
- **impact** — A uv failure costs a heavy forced reinstall (torch/faiss for Cognee) on every rebuild, and a fix to one copy misses the other two.
- **closes** — Extract the installer into one function under modules/stacks/ai-agents/ (or a uvTools executor if install ownership moves to the channel), move the three call sites onto it, and have it check uv's exit status.
- **rule** — Abstraction before addition (Rule 1)
- **node** — `01M3E9TMG3C90N8VBEDXGHHK45`

### GAP: tldraw canvases are tied to the machine that holds the file

- **expected** — Canvases live on a tldraw offline-server on shared-server, placed with my.services, so any machine opens or joins them live; canvas-link open works across hosts.
- **current** — tldraw offline v1.23.0 stable ships no offline-server (nightly-only, preview-licensed); canvas-link records each canvas's host and open answers 'on <host>' for other machines.
- **impact** — A canvas linked from one Mac cannot be opened from another Mac or from shared-server threads.
- **closes** — When tldraw offline ships offlineServer in a stable release: place it via my.services on shared-server and teach canvas-link open to join it.
- **node** — `01M5M0X6NAE1AMVDKCSG41E0NP`

### GAP: two scripts read Nix settings by scraping source with awk

- **expected** — Scripts read declared state one way: evaluating the host configuration, as the drift audit already does for every package channel.
- **current** — audit-system-discrepancies.sh parse_external_paths awk-scrapes managedPaths from external-workspace.nix and hard-codes its root /Volumes/Data/workspace/symlinks/User; check-kb-assets-backup.sh awk-scrapes mackup.nix for the storage engine and allowlist.
- **impact** — Reformatting either Nix file, or computing the list, silently changes what the scripts see, and the audit's root literal can drift from externalDataRoot.
- **closes** — Expose managedPaths and externalDataRoot (and the mackup settings) as read-only options and read them with eval_host_list; keep check-kb-assets-backup.sh's pre-commit speed in mind before moving it to nix eval.
- **rule** — Abstraction before addition (Rule 1)
- **node** — `01M3E9VYK1NK02TN5MYSQXS7C7`


## Closed

### GAP: bb plugins stay stale when Home Manager activation is interrupted

- **expected** — Every rebuild leaves each declared bb plugin installed at its current source; an interrupted activation is redone by the next rebuild.
- **current** — installBbPlugins runs only in Home Manager activation. When it is cut off (2026-10-24 10:09 power-key poweroff mid-switch), the next rebuild yields the same system closure, home-manager-<user>.service is unchanged and not restarted, so plugin stamps stay old (bbim v2 was not installed until activation was rerun by hand).
- **impact** — A merged plugin change silently does not reach bb; nothing reports it.
- **closes** — Run the bb plugin installer on every rebuild (or at boot) regardless of closure change, or have rebuild/restart-app --status report plugins whose stamp differs from their source.
- **node** — `01M5P3ET7FV0S3JJ7DH50EHNY4`

### GAP: bb-lively cannot ship a font face; presets name system and OFL families that show only if installed

- **expected** — A preset's OFL faces (Cloudbank: Jost, Josefin Sans; kb ships them from @fontsource) load in bb whatever the machine has installed
- **current** — bb-lively names families only; no route or bundle serves a font file, so Cloudbank falls back to Avenir Next and Futura (macOS) or the system sans
- **impact** — Cloudbank's lettering and body type differ by machine and from kb's Transistor
- **closes** — Closed by installing the faces on the Macs, where bb is viewed: nix-darwin fonts.packages in the bb stack (modules/stacks/bb/darwin.nix). Serving @fontsource woff2 files from the plugin would still reach other devices (a phone)
- **node** — `01M5SK4NQ90CRG9YAQC2GXNZJW`

- **current** — bbim declines in a browser tab (its isAvailable is false there and bare keys stay off), so the tab's own keys work but nothing is hintable; the hint-bridge script covers only pages that load it
- **impact** — keyboard-only navigation stops at the browser tab boundary
- **closes** — assets/bb-plugins/bbim/adapter/bb.ts gains a browser-tab injector that runs the core's collect/activate in the page, and the GAP comment there goes

### GAP: two launch paths for the kb binary
